messages.author: f06db63329fab1f9
messages.subject: Re: Optimizations.java issue?
parts:
This exception is thrown by the nlm() method when one of the parameters is "missing", i.e. Double.NaN:

https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin/blob/c724b7b2ef7abfa45fb0d57796dd11177a7973fd/core/src/main/java/org/renjin/stats/internals/optimize/Optimizations.java#L234-L234

This could be caused either by a problem with your data, or a problem with some function in Renjin that is returning a missing value instead of something else. 

Can you try running your code in GNU R? If you don't get the same error, please open a bug report at 
https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin/issues

with a small test case that can be used to reproduce the error.

Thanks,

Alex

messages.author: f06db63329fab1f9
messages.subject: Re: Optimizations.java issue?
parts:
No, NaN treatment is the same, but often what happens is that there is a bug somewhere in Renjin somewhere that generates an NA instead of the correct value, and then this value gets passed around for a few function calls until it finally hits a function that checks its' inputs, at which point an error is thrown.

This makes it hard to debug because the site of the actual bug can be miles away from the function that finally throws an error. 

If you can boil down your script to something trivial, perhaps just the first 3 rows of your dataset with masked column names, for example, then you can open an issue on GitHub and I can take a closer look.

Best,
Alex

messages.subject: Re: Optimizations.java issue?
parts:
The error is being thrown because the 'p' argument has an NA value. So something is going wrong in whatever is getting assigned to init.pars.

Also looking again at the stack trace, it looks like you're not using the latest version of Renjin. Can you tell me what version you are using? The latest is 0.8.2003.

Best,
Alex

On Friday, April 29, 2016 at 6:56:45 AM UTC-7, Alexander Bertram wrote:
No, NaN treatment is the same, but often what happens is that there is a bug somewhere in Renjin somewhere that generates an NA instead of the correct value, and then this value gets passed around for a few function calls until it finally hits a function that checks its' inputs, at which point an error is thrown.

This makes it hard to debug because the site of the actual bug can be miles away from the function that finally throws an error. 

If you can boil down your script to something trivial, perhaps just the first 3 rows of your dataset with masked column names, for example, then you can open an issue on GitHub and I can take a closer look.

Best,
Alex
